rationale.conceptual: Requires understanding of DFT setup (pseudopotentials, k-points, cutoffs, variable-cell relaxation) and formation energy computation. While not a novel custom method, it demands careful implementation of a well-known but multi-parameter algorithm that is not trivial for a non-expert.
rationale.execution: The workflow involves 4–5 DFT runs (graphene, symmetric graphane, anti-symmetric graphane, strained graphane), plus extraction of geometric parameters and energies. Environment setup (Quantum ESPRESSO, pseudopotentials) adds some orchestration complexity, but each step is a single pw.x run and there are no fragile data-fetching or multi-tool handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves standard plane-wave DFT geometry optimizations of small graphene/graphane unit cells using an established code (Quantum ESPRESSO). The conceptual method is non-trivial but well-documented; execution is a ~4-stage pipeline with tool setup and sequential runs. Resource needs are minimal: tiny unit cells, CPU-only, low memory.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Unit cells contain only 2 carbon atoms (graphene) or 2 carbon + 2 hydrogen atoms (graphane); k-point mesh 16×16×1 and plane-wave cutoffs 30/240 Ry. This is a tiny DFT calculation that runs quickly on a single CPU core with negligible memory and no external data beyond pseudopotential files.
